questions.q: For an innovation to be successful, it must
options: be advertised effectively.
address the needs of users.
have a registered trademark.
be launched at an appropriate time.
questions.explanation: A successful innovation must meet a genuine user need, otherwise consumers will not adopt it regardless of marketing. Advertising, trademarks and timing are TEMPLE factors that support an innovation but cannot make it succeed if it fails to address user needs.

questions.q: Which combination of factors is the most important for a designer to consider when developing a new app?
options: Political and legal implications
Marketing strategies and timing
Economic and historical influences
Cultural impact and emerging technologies
questions.explanation: In a fast-moving software market the success of a new app depends most on the marketing strategy and the timing of its release so it reaches users ahead of competitors. The other TEMPLE factors are relevant but secondary to getting the product to market effectively — exactly the lesson of the Zune arriving after the iPod had locked up the market.

questions.q: According to the episode, which enabling technologies made the Flow Hive's complex plastic honeycomb frames manufacturable?
options: Three-D printing for prototyping and injection moulding for production
CNC milling of metal frames and hand assembly
Laser cutting of timber and traditional beeswax moulding
Vacuum forming and blow moulding of glass
questions.explanation: This is the 'E' in TEMPLE — emerging and available technologies. The episode states the complex honeycomb-splitting frames could only be manufactured using three-D printing for prototyping and injection moulding for production.

questions.q: In the episode, why is the Apple Newton used as an example of an innovation that failed?
options: It was launched too early, before the enabling technology was mature and before consumers were ready
It was patented too late, so competitors copied the idea
It was over-marketed until consumers grew sceptical of it
Its manufacturing costs were far too high for any market
questions.explanation: The Newton failed on the 'T' of TEMPLE — timing. It was a good idea launched before the enabling technology was ready and before society was ready, so its poor timing contributed to its failure. Same six factors, failure when they do not align.

questions.q: What is the most common HSC error the episode warns about regarding the TEMPLE factors?
options: Confusing the six innovation-success factors (TEMPLE, H3.1) with the eleven factors affecting design (FFA EQ NEW LOAd, H1.1)
Using the Flow Hive as a failure example instead of a success
Listing only two TEMPLE factors instead of all six
Believing that timing is never examined in the written paper
questions.explanation: The headline trap is mixing up the two lists. The eleven design factors (function, aesthetics, ergonomics and so on) judge whether the design itself is good; the six TEMPLE factors judge whether an innovation succeeds in the world. A paper often asks both, so you must know which is which.

questions.q: From memory, what do the six letters of TEMPLE — the factors of innovation success — stand for?
keyPoints: T — Timing: launching at the right moment, when society is ready.
E — Emerging and available technologies: the technologies that make the innovation possible.
M — Marketing strategies: how it is promoted and sold.
P — Political factors: government support, regulation and the political climate.
L — Legal and economic factors: patents and intellectual property, cost and economic conditions.
E — Era: the historical and cultural influences of the time.
questions.explanation: An innovation succeeds inside a TEMPLE. If you recalled all six, you are ready for the most examined idea in module H2; if a couple slipped, drill them — this framework is the spine of nearly every Section three answer.

questions.q: In your own words, why do the same six TEMPLE factors explain both the success AND the failure of an innovation?
keyPoints: An innovation succeeds when the factors align in its favour and fails when one or more go against it.
The Flow Hive succeeded because timing, technology, marketing and legal protection all lined up.
The Zune failed on timing and marketing (it arrived after the iPod had locked up the market); the Newton failed on timing and immature technology.
questions.explanation: The power of TEMPLE is that one framework explains both outcomes. When you analyse, don't just say 'it succeeded' — identify which TEMPLE factors drove the outcome, and lead with the two or three that were decisive.

questions.q: Why are some innovative products more successful than others?
questions.modelAnswer: Some innovative products are more successful because of the timing of their release, the designer's ability to address current trends, and how well they solve a real or genuine need. Other factors such as improved capabilities, ease of use and improved quality also affect the success of an innovative design.

criteria.descriptor: Provides reasons why some innovative products are more successful

questions.explanation: This is a 2-mark version of the TEMPLE idea: name factors such as timing, addressing current trends (era/marketing) and solving a genuine user need, and give the reason they matter.

questions.q:
There is growing consumer demand for innovative products that enhance the quality of life.

Explain a range of factors that contribute to the success of these products.

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident between a range of factors and the contribution to the success of innovations and enhancement of life quality
Provides characteristics and features of factors that contribute to the success of innovations and demonstrates a link to enhance quality of life
Sketches in general terms a factor that contributes to the success of innovations OR indicates the features of successful innovations
Identifies a factor that contributes to the success of innovations

questions.explanation: Walk a range of the TEMPLE factors — timing, emerging and available technologies, marketing strategies, political, legal and economic factors, and era — and show how each contributes to success, linking back to enhancing quality of life. Use the Flow Hive (timing with the save-the-bees movement, injection moulding, a record crowdfunding campaign, a patent filed before crowdfunding) as worked detail rather than asserting 'it was a good idea'.

questions.q: Analyse how economic, historical and timing factors determine the success or failure of designs.
questions.modelAnswer: Economic, historical and timing factors all strongly determine whether a design succeeds or fails. Economically, a product released during a negative climate of high interest rates and low disposable income is less likely to be embraced, so designers must time release to a positive climate or to when the product is most needed — for example launching a Dyson air fan in the warmer spring and summer season, when consumers prioritise cooling even in tough economic times, rather than in winter at a high price. Governments may also provide incentives, financial support and favourable trade conditions in poor periods, improving the economic viability of design and production. Yet some designs succeed regardless of high purchase and upgrade costs: Apple phones and music devices dominate the market because effective marketing makes them perceived as needed and essential, showing that perceived need and timing of release can outweigh pure economic viability. Together these economic, historical and timing factors determine not only sales to the target market but also the broader acceptance and desirability of a design in society.

criteria.descriptor: Draws out and relates implications of how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Provides reasons through the use of cause and effect as to how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Identifies issues and provides evidence of how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Provides characteristics and features of how at least TWO of these factors (economic, historical and timing) affect the success or failure of designs
Sketches in general terms how economic and/or historical and/or timing factors affect the success and/or failure of designs
Identifies a feature of economic or historical or timing factors that affects the success and/or failure of designs

questions.explanation: These three are TEMPLE factors (Legal-and-economic, Era/historical, and Timing). A top answer weighs them with cause and effect and contrasts a success with a failure on the same factor — for example the Flow Hive's perfect timing with the save-the-bees movement against the Apple Newton, which launched too early.
